ai_show_review.summary: Jazz‑infused suite with stellar Clementine, New Potato and rare Spanish Jam
ai_show_review.blurb: Features the first ever performance of "Clementine" alongside a soaring New Potato Caboose and a smoky Spanish Jam. The set flows like one continuous composition, highlighted by tight transitions into Born Cross‑Eyed, Caution and a Dark Star fragment. All five soundboard sources capture the band at a high‑energy, swing‑filled peak.
ai_show_review.review: The Eureka Municipal Auditorium show delivers an almost orchestral jazz suite that stands out as one of the most sophisticated early‑1968 performances. From the opening jam into "Clementine"—the song’s debut—the band moves seamlessly into a spacious New Potato Caboose where Garcia’s guitar glows like “bassy tubes” and Pigpen’s organ adds rich, swinging texture. Phil Lesh’s Coltrane‑inspired bass underpins the flow into Born Cross‑Eyed, then a feedback‑laden bridge that launches straight into a mesmerizing Spanish Jam and a brief but thrilling Caution before a fragment of Dark Star caps the set. The rhythm section—Mickey Hart’s jazzy ride and Bill Kreutzmann’s driving fills—keeps everything tight yet exploratory, making the whole hour feel like one long, cohesive composition.

best_recording.reason: Excellent soundboard capture with crystal‑clear mix and flawless instrument separation, showcasing every nuance of the jazzy suite.

key_highlights: First ever performance of "Clementine" delivered with soaring vocals and spacious guitar.
New Potato Caboose and Spanish Jam flow together in a seamless, swing‑filled groove.
Rare Born Cross‑Eyed → Caution transition highlighted by bass‑driven leads.
All five soundboard recordings are excellent; the Clugston source is the clearest.

band_performance.Jerry: Spacious New Potato tone, glowing solo work on Spanish Jam and Clementine; also provides lead vocals on "Clementine".
band_performance.Phil: Writer of "Clementine", delivers Coltrane‑inspired bass lines that drive the jazzy transitions, especially strong at the start of Caution.
band_performance.Mickey: Swinging, jazz‑inflected drumming that propels the set’s groove and adds subtle accents throughout.
band_performance.Billy: Provides a solid, driving foundation alongside Mickey; his fills help keep the high‑energy flow tight.
